## What this document shows

Every run here has its **own independent seed** (drawn once with
`draw_seeds()` from `measles_model.R`), so runs are never compared one by one.
Everything is a **summary over all runs** of a scenario:

| Exhibit | Question it answers | Where in the paper |
|---|---|---|
| T1, C0, C6 | How long is each disease stage in the model, and how does that compare with real measles? | Methods / Supplement |
| C1 | What does the *average* infected student go through, day by day? | Results (model behaviour) |
| C2 | Where are contagious days spent: at school or at home? | Results (mechanism) |
| R1 | After *q* days at home, what is the chance an infected student has still not had the rash, in the model and in real measles? | Methods / Discussion (the key model property) |
| R2, C4 | Per outbreak: how many infected students are sent home, how many come back still infected, and how many contagious days they then spend at school | Results / Discussion (why the strategies differ) |
| C5 | How much of a student's contagious period does quarantine cover? | Discussion |

**How to report numbers.**

- *Spread between students* (how variable the disease course is): **median (5th95th percentile)**, e.g. "latent period: median 8 days (5th95th percentile 134)".
- *An average over runs* (how precisely it is estimated): **mean (95% CI)**, e.g. "students released still infected: 6.6 per outbreak (95% CI 6.36.9)".

::: {.callout-note}
Quick test: `N_RUNS=50 quarto render 09_model_behaviour.qmd`.
Simulations are cached in `results/09_behaviour2_*.rds`; delete them to re-run.
:::

```{r setup}
source("measles_model.R")
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)

## ---- Settings ---------------------------------------------------------------
N_RUNS     <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("N_RUNS", unset = 1000))  # independent runs per school x strategy
SEED_BEHAV <- SEED + 9L      # its own seed, so these runs are independent of the runs in 01
STRATS     <- c("21/21/21", "21/14/14", "21/14/7", "21/7/7", "21/0/0")
VACC       <- 0.70           # vaccination coverage used in this document
PROG_STRAT <- "21/21/21"     # strategy used for the disease-progression table (T1, C0, C6)
MIN_HOME   <- 7              # days in a row at home that count as a "real" quarantine
## Real measles, for R1: infection -> symptom onset is log-normal with median
## 12.5 days and dispersion 1.23 (Lessler et al. 2009, Lancet Infect Dis);
## the rash follows about 3 days later (prodrome 2-4 days).
REAL_MEDIAN   <- 12.5
REAL_DISP     <- 1.23
REAL_PRODROME <- 3
Q_MARKS       <- c(1, 7, 14, 21)   # quarantine lengths marked in R1 (0-day quarantine = 1 day at home)
MAX_K      <- 40             # days after infection drawn in C1

COLS <- setNames(c("#1F4E79", "#3A7DBA", "#7FB2DE", "#E8A33D", "#C8531E"), STRATS)
th <- theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title.position = "plot", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
save_fig <- function(p, file, w, h) {
  dir.create(FIG_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, file), p, width = w, height = h, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  p
}
dir.create(RESULTS_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

```{r functions}
## ---- Model with a daily state recorder -------------------------------------
rec <- new.env()
build_model <- function(school, vacc, duration) {
  sizes <- ENROLLMENT[[school]]; n <- sum(sizes)
  m <- ModelMeaslesMixingRiskQuarantine(
    n = n, prevalence = 1 / n,
    contact_matrix = SCHOOL_CMAT[[school]], transmission_rate = TRANS_RATE[[school]],
    prop_vaccinated = vacc, detection_rate_quarantine = 0.0,
    contact_tracing_days_window = 7,
    quarantine_period_high   = as.integer(duration[1]),
    quarantine_period_medium = as.integer(duration[2]),
    quarantine_period_low    = as.integer(duration[3]))
  for (k in seq_along(sizes))
    m <- add_entity(m, entity("Grade", as.integer(sizes[k]), FALSE))
  f  <- function(m) rec$days[[length(rec$days) + 1L]] <- get_agents_states(m)
  ge <- globalevent_fun(f, "State recorder")
  rec$keep[[length(rec$keep) + 1L]] <- list(f, ge, m)   # keep R from garbage-collecting it
  m <- add_globalevent(m, ge)
  verbose_off(m)
  m
}
parse_strat <- function(s) as.integer(strsplit(s, "/")[[1]])
longest_run <- function(x) if (!length(x) || !any(x)) 0L else { r <- rle(x); max(r$lengths[r$values]) }

QSTATES  <- c("Quarantined Susceptible", "Quarantined Latent", "Quarantined Prodromal", "Quarantined Recovered")
CONTAG   <- c("Prodromal", "Quarantined Prodromal")
RASHLIKE <- c("Rash", "Isolated", "Isolated Recovered", "Hospitalized")
NOTICED  <- c("Isolated", "Isolated Recovered", "Hospitalized")
CATS <- c("Latent, at school", "Latent, at home", "Contagious, at school",
          "Contagious, at home", "Rash / isolated / hospital", "Recovered")
cat_state <- function(x) fcase(x == "Latent", CATS[1], x == "Quarantined Latent", CATS[2],
                               x == "Prodromal", CATS[3], x == "Quarantined Prodromal", CATS[4],
                               x %in% RASHLIKE, CATS[5], default = CATS[6])

## ---- One run -> small summaries --------------------------------------------
one_run <- function(m, seed) {
  rec$days <- list()
  run(m, ndays = N_DAYS, seed = seed)
  S  <- do.call(rbind, rec$days); nd <- nrow(S)
  tr <- as.data.table(get_transmissions(m))[, .(date, source, target)]
  isQ <- matrix(S %in% QSTATES, nd)

  ## first detection: first day a rash is noticed (isolated, or straight to hospital);
  ## the first students are sent home that same day
  det <- which(rowSums(S == "Isolated" | S == "Isolated Recovered" | isQ) > 0)
  fd  <- if (length(det)) min(det) else NA_integer_

  ## infected students (first case excluded): stage durations and longest stay at home
  inf <- tr[source >= 0]
  st <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(inf)), function(k) {
    i <- inf$target[k] + 1L; d0 <- inf$date[k]; x <- S[, i]; after <- seq_len(nd) > d0
    cd <- which(x %in% CONTAG); rd <- which(x %in% RASHLIKE & after); nt <- which(x %in% NOTICED & after)
    ## first stay at home while infected: when it started, and how it ended
    qi <- x %in% c("Quarantined Latent", "Quarantined Prodromal")
    s0 <- if (any(qi)) which(qi)[1] else NA_integer_
    e0 <- if (is.na(s0)) NA_integer_ else { r <- which(!qi & seq_len(nd) > s0); if (length(r)) min(r) - 1L else nd }
    back_inf <- !is.na(e0) && e0 < nd && x[e0 + 1L] %in% c("Latent", "Prodromal")   # back at school, still infected
    data.table(
      home_state      = if (is.na(s0)) NA_character_ else x[s0],      # state on the first day at home
      since_inf       = s0 - d0,                                       # days since infection when sent home
      rash_after_home = if (is.na(s0) || !length(rd)) NA_real_ else min(rd) - s0,  # days at home until the rash
      home_late       = !is.na(s0) && s0 > N_DAYS - 45,                # too close to the end to follow up
      back_inf        = back_inf,
      back_contag     = if (back_inf) sum(x[(e0 + 1L):nd] == "Prodromal") else 0L,
      latent          = if (length(cd)) min(cd) - d0 else NA_real_,
      contagious      = if (length(cd)) length(cd) else NA_real_,
      contag_home     = sum(x == "Quarantined Prodromal"),
      inf_to_rash     = if (length(rd)) min(rd) - d0 else NA_real_,
      rash_to_noticed = if (length(rd) && length(nt) && x[min(rd)] == "Rash") min(nt) - min(rd) else NA_real_,
      stay            = longest_run(x %in% c("Quarantined Latent", "Quarantined Prodromal")))
  }))

  ## C1: state and place on each day since infection (counts)
  jc <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(inf)), function(k) {
    i <- inf$target[k] + 1L; d0 <- inf$date[k]; days <- d0:min(nd, d0 + MAX_K)
    data.table(k = days - d0, cat = cat_state(S[days, i]))
  }))
  jc <- if (nrow(jc)) jc[, .N, by = .(k, cat)] else data.table(k = integer(), cat = character(), N = integer())

  ## C2: contagious student-days at school before / after the first detection, and at home
  pr <- S == "Prodromal"
  cd <- data.table(before = if (is.na(fd)) sum(pr) else sum(pr[seq_len(fd), ]),
                   after  = if (is.na(fd)) 0 else sum(pr[-seq_len(fd), , drop = FALSE]),
                   home   = sum(S == "Quarantined Prodromal"))

  ## R2 / C4: one row per outbreak (runs are independent, so these have valid CIs)
  cd[, `:=`(size         = nrow(tr),
            sent_inf     = if (nrow(st)) sum(!is.na(st$home_state)) else 0L,   # infected students sent home
            back_inf     = if (nrow(st)) sum(st$back_inf) else 0L,             # ... who came back still infected
            back_contag  = if (nrow(st)) sum(st$back_contag) else 0L)]         # their contagious days at school after
  list(st = st, jc = jc, cd = cd)
}

## ---- One scenario (school x strategy): all its runs, in parallel, cached ------
behaviour_scenario <- function(school, strategy, seeds) {
  f <- file.path(RESULTS_DIR, sprintf("09_behaviour2_%s_%d_%s_n%d_seed%d.rds",
                                      school, round(100 * VACC), gsub("/", "-", strategy),
                                      length(seeds), SEED_BEHAV))
  if (file.exists(f)) return(readRDS(f))
  run_chunk <- function(s) {
    m <- build_model(school, VACC, parse_strat(strategy))
    lapply(s, function(sd) one_run(m, sd))
  }
  ncores <- max(1L, min(N_THREADS, length(seeds)))
  chunks <- split(seeds, ceiling(seq_along(seeds) / ceiling(length(seeds) / ncores)))
  out <- unlist(parallel::mclapply(chunks, run_chunk, mc.cores = ncores), recursive = FALSE)
  tag <- function(d) d[, `:=`(school = school, strategy = strategy)]
  res <- list(
    st = tag(rbindlist(lapply(out, `[[`, "st"))),
    jc = tag(rbindlist(lapply(out, `[[`, "jc"))[, .(N = sum(N)), by = .(k, cat)]),
    cd = tag(rbindlist(lapply(out, `[[`, "cd"))),
    n_runs = length(seeds))
  saveRDS(res, f)
  res
}
```

```{r simulate}
## One seed per run, all drawn at once without repeats: every run of every
## school x strategy is independent.
scen  <- CJ(school = SCHOOLS, strategy = STRATS, sorted = FALSE)
seeds <- draw_seeds(nrow(scen), N_RUNS, SEED_BEHAV)
R <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(scen)), function(j) behaviour_scenario(scen$school[j], scen$strategy[j], seeds[[j]]))

ST <- rbindlist(lapply(R, `[[`, "st")); JC <- rbindlist(lapply(R, `[[`, "jc"))
CD <- rbindlist(lapply(R, `[[`, "cd"))
for (d in list(ST, JC, CD)) d[, `:=`(school = factor(school, SCHOOLS), strategy = factor(strategy, STRATS))]
```

Each school × strategy has **`r N_RUNS` independent runs** at
**`r vacc_lab(VACC)`** vaccination coverage, `r N_DAYS` days each.
Durations are measured on infected students other than the first case, and only
for students whose stage ended within the `r N_DAYS` simulated days.

## T1. Disease progression in the model

```{r t1}
summ <- function(v, lab, real) {
  v <- v[!is.na(v)]; m <- mean(v); se <- sd(v) / sqrt(length(v))
  data.table(Stage = lab, Students = length(v), `Median (days)` = median(v),
             `5th-95th percentile` = sprintf("%g-%g", quantile(v, .05, type = 1), quantile(v, .95, type = 1)),
             `Mean (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", m, m - 1.96 * se, m + 1.96 * se),
             `Real measles` = real)
}
T1 <- ST[strategy == PROG_STRAT, rbind(
  summ(latent,          "Infection to contagious (latent)",     "about 10-12 days"),
  summ(contagious,      "Contagious, before rash (prodromal)",  "about 4 days (2-4)"),
  summ(inf_to_rash,     "Infection to rash",                    "about 14 days (7-21)"),
  summ(rash_to_noticed, "Rash at school to noticed",            "-")), by = school]
setnames(T1, "school", "School")
fwrite(T1, file.path(RESULTS_DIR, sprintf("09_T1_progression_n%d_seed%d.csv", N_RUNS, SEED_BEHAV)))
knitr::kable(T1, align = "llrrrrl",
             caption = sprintf("Disease progression in the model (%s, %s vaccinated). Median and 5th-95th percentile describe how much the course varies between students; mean (95%% CI) is the average and its precision.",
                               PROG_STRAT, vacc_lab(VACC)))
```

**How to write it.** "In the model, the latent period had a median of X days
(5th95th percentile AB), compared with about 1012 days for measles. Because
each stage has a geometric duration (the same chance of moving on every day),
the model produces many very short and some very long stages."

## C0. Stage lengths compared with real measles

```{r c0, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
rng <- melt(ST[strategy == PROG_STRAT], id.vars = "school",
            measure.vars = c("latent", "contagious", "inf_to_rash"),
            variable.name = "stage", value.name = "days")[!is.na(days)]
rng <- rng[, .(med = median(days), mean = mean(days),
               lo = quantile(days, .05, type = 1), hi = quantile(days, .95, type = 1),
               q1 = quantile(days, .25, type = 1), q3 = quantile(days, .75, type = 1)), by = .(school, stage)]
STAGE_LAB <- c(contagious = "Contagious period", latent = "Infection to contagious", inf_to_rash = "Infection to rash")
rng[, yy := match(as.character(stage), names(STAGE_LAB))]
real <- data.table(yy = 1:3, lo = c(2, 10, 7), hi = c(4, 12, 21))
p <- ggplot(rng, aes(y = yy)) +
  geom_rect(data = real, aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, ymin = yy - 0.35, ymax = yy + 0.35),
            fill = "#D9EAD3", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), linewidth = 1, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = q1, xmax = q3), linewidth = 4, colour = "#3A7DBA") +
  geom_point(aes(x = med), size = 3, colour = "white") +
  geom_point(aes(x = mean), shape = 4, size = 3, stroke = 1.2) +
  geom_text(aes(x = hi, label = sprintf("  %g-%g", lo, hi)), hjust = 0, size = 3.3) +
  facet_wrap(~school, ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:3, labels = unname(STAGE_LAB)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = "Days", y = NULL,
       title = "How long each stage lasts in the model, compared with real measles",
       subtitle = sprintf("Blue = middle 50%%, grey line = 5th-95th percentile (labelled), white dot = median, x = mean; green = typical real range. %s.", PROG_STRAT)) + th
save_fig(p, "09_C0_progression_ranges.png", 10, 6)
```

## C6. Days from infection to rash

```{r c6, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
c6 <- ST[strategy == PROG_STRAT & !is.na(inf_to_rash)]
out <- c6[, .(lab = sprintf("%.0f%% outside 7-21 days", 100 * mean(!between(inf_to_rash, 7, 21)))), by = school]
p <- ggplot(c6, aes(inf_to_rash)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 7, xmax = 21, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#D9EAD3") +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), binwidth = 1, fill = "#3A7DBA", colour = "white") +
  geom_text(data = out, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = lab), hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5) +
  facet_wrap(~school, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 60)) +
  labs(x = "Days from infection to rash", y = "Share of infected students",
       title = "Days from infection to rash: model vs real measles (green = 7-21 days)",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s, %s vaccinated", PROG_STRAT, vacc_lab(VACC))) + th
save_fig(p, "09_C6_infection_to_rash.png", 10, 4.5)
```

## C1. The average infected student, day by day

For every infected student, day 0 is the day of infection. Each colour is the
share of all infected students (all runs) in that state and place on that day.
Only the red band, **contagious at school**, can infect anyone.

```{r c1, fig.width=13, fig.height=8}
## fill missing state/day combinations with 0 so the stacked areas line up
JC <- JC[CJ(school = levels(JC$school), strategy = levels(JC$strategy), k = 0:MAX_K, cat = CATS),
         on = .(school, strategy, k, cat)][is.na(N), N := 0]
JC[, `:=`(school = factor(school, SCHOOLS), strategy = factor(strategy, STRATS))]
JC[, share := N / sum(N), by = .(school, strategy, k)][, cat := factor(cat, CATS)]
p <- ggplot(JC, aes(k, share, fill = cat)) + geom_area() +
  facet_grid(school ~ strategy) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#BDBDBD", "#F3E3C3", "#C8531E", "#F2A27A", "#7A6FD0", "#E8EEF4"),
                    name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Days since the student was infected", y = "Share of infected students",
       title = "The average infected student: state and place, day by day after infection",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s vaccinated. Red = contagious at school (the only days that spread measles)", vacc_lab(VACC))) + th
save_fig(p, "09_C1_average_journey.png", 13, 8)
```

## C2. Where contagious days are spent

```{r c2, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
CD_LAB <- c(before = "At school, before first detection", after = "At school, after first detection",
            home = "At home (quarantine)")
c2 <- melt(CD[, lapply(.SD, mean), by = .(school, strategy), .SDcols = names(CD_LAB)],
           id.vars = c("school", "strategy"))
c2[, variable := factor(CD_LAB[as.character(variable)], CD_LAB)][, strategy := factor(strategy, rev(STRATS))]
p <- ggplot(c2, aes(value, strategy, fill = variable)) + geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  facet_wrap(~school, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#B4B2A9", "#C8531E", "#F2D9A6"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Contagious student-days per outbreak (average over all runs)", y = NULL,
       title = "Where contagious days are spent", subtitle = "Only contagious days at school can infect others") + th
save_fig(p, "09_C2_contagious_days.png", 10, 7)

## the same numbers with 95% CI, for the text
ci <- function(v) { m <- mean(v); h <- 1.96 * sd(v) / sqrt(length(v)); sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", m, m - h, m + h) }
knitr::kable(CD[, .(`At school, before detection` = ci(before), `At school, after detection` = ci(after),
                    `At home` = ci(home), `Outbreak size` = ci(size)), by = .(School = school, Strategy = strategy)],
             caption = "Contagious student-days per outbreak, mean (95% CI).")
```

## R1. Will an infected student still be infected when quarantine ends? Model vs real measles

This is the property of the model that explains most of the results.

For every infected student sent home **while still latent**, we count the days
from their first day at home until their rash. The question is: after *q* days
at home, what share have **still not had the rash**? Those students would
return to school on day *q* still infected, and become contagious there.

- **Model (solid lines, from the simulations):** each day a latent student
  becomes contagious with the same chance (1/12), so the time *still to go* does not
  depend on how long ago the student was infected. Students sent home 03, 47
  or 8+ days after infection give nearly the same curve.
- **Real measles (dashed lines):** infection to symptoms is log-normal (median
  `r REAL_MEDIAN` days, dispersion `r REAL_DISP`), with the rash about
  `r REAL_PRODROME` days later. A student infected a while ago is close to the rash, so
  the time still to go *does* depend on when they were infected, and almost no one
  is still pre-rash 21 days after exposure. That is why 21 days is the
  standard quarantine.

```{r r1, fig.width=10, fig.height=5.5}
## model: empirical, from all students sent home while latent (all schools and strategies)
lat <- ST[home_state == "Quarantined Latent" & !home_late]
lat[, grp := cut(since_inf, c(-Inf, 3, 7, Inf), labels = c("0-3", "4-7", "8+"))]
QQ <- 0:35
model <- lat[, .(q = QQ, surv = vapply(QQ, function(q) mean(is.na(rash_after_home) | rash_after_home >= q), 0), n = .N), by = grp]

## real measles: P(T > e + q | T > e), T = REAL_PRODROME + log-normal(median, dispersion)
E_REP <- c("0-3" = 2, "4-7" = 6, "8+" = 10)        # a typical day since infection for each group
real_surv <- function(t) plnorm(t - REAL_PRODROME, log(REAL_MEDIAN), log(REAL_DISP), lower.tail = FALSE)
real <- rbindlist(lapply(names(E_REP), function(g) { e <- E_REP[[g]]
  data.table(grp = g, q = QQ, surv = real_surv(e + QQ) / real_surv(e)) }))
both <- rbind(model[, .(grp, q, surv, source = "Model")], real[, .(grp, q, surv, source = "Real measles")])
N_GRP <- lat[, .N, keyby = grp][J(names(E_REP)), N]       # students in each group (model)
N_GRP[is.na(N_GRP)] <- 0L
GRP_LAB <- sprintf("sent home %s days after infection (n = %d)", names(E_REP), N_GRP)
both[, grp := factor(grp, names(E_REP), GRP_LAB)]

lab21 <- both[q == 21, .(surv = mean(surv)), by = source]
p <- ggplot(both, aes(q, surv, colour = grp, linetype = source)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = Q_MARKS, colour = "grey80") +
  annotate("text", x = Q_MARKS, y = 1.04, label = paste(Q_MARKS, "d"), size = 3.2, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("label", x = 21.5, y = lab21[source == "Model", surv] + 0.08, hjust = 0, size = 3.4,
           label = sprintf("Model: %.0f%% still pre-rash after 21 days", 100 * lab21[source == "Model", surv])) +
  annotate("label", x = 21.5, y = 0.06, hjust = 0, size = 3.4,
           label = sprintf("Real measles: %.1f%%", 100 * lab21[source == "Real measles", surv])) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#1F4E79", "#E8A33D", "#C8531E"), name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Model = "solid", `Real measles` = "dashed"), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1.06)) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1), linetype = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Days at home (quarantine length)", y = "Share still without rash\n(would return to school infected)",
       title = "Chance that a student sent home while latent is still pre-rash after q days at home",
       subtitle = "Model: the same curve whenever the student was infected. Real measles: falls to almost 0 by 21 days.") + th +
  theme(legend.box = "vertical")
save_fig(p, "09_R1_still_infected_after_q.png", 10, 5.5)

## the numbers at the marked quarantine lengths
r1 <- dcast(both[q %in% Q_MARKS, .(surv = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * surv)), by = .(grp, source, q)],
            source + grp ~ q, value.var = "surv")
r1[, grp := as.character(grp)][source == "Real measles", grp := sub(" \\(n = .*\\)", "", grp)]  # real = calculated, no n
setnames(r1, c("source", "grp", as.character(Q_MARKS)), c("", "Group", paste(Q_MARKS, "days at home")))
knitr::kable(r1, caption = sprintf("Share still without rash after q days at home. Model: %d students sent home while latent, all schools and strategies (n per group in the Group column). Real measles: calculated, no students.", nrow(lat)))

## how many students in each group, by school and strategy
n_tab <- dcast(lat[, .N, by = .(School = school, Strategy = strategy, grp)],
               School + Strategy ~ grp, value.var = "N", fill = 0)
n_tab[, Total := rowSums(.SD), .SDcols = setdiff(names(n_tab), c("School", "Strategy"))]
setnames(n_tab, names(E_REP), sprintf("Sent home %s days after infection", names(E_REP)), skip_absent = TRUE)
knitr::kable(n_tab, caption = sprintf("Students sent home while latent, used in R1 (%d runs per school x strategy).", N_RUNS))
```

**How to write it.** "Each disease stage in the model has a geometric
duration, so the time an infected student still has to go before the rash
does not depend on how long ago they were infected. After 21 days at home,
X% of students quarantined while latent had still not developed a rash,
compared with under 1% expected for measles. These students return to school
infected, which limits the benefit of longer quarantines (R2)."

## R2. Per outbreak: infected students sent home, and how many came back still infected

One number per outbreak, and outbreaks are independent runs, so the 95% CIs
are valid.

```{r r2}
ci <- function(v) { m <- mean(v); h <- 1.96 * sd(v) / sqrt(length(v)); sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", m, m - h, m + h) }
r2 <- CD[, .(`Outbreak size` = ci(size),
             `Infected students sent home` = ci(sent_inf),
             `... came back still infected` = ci(back_inf),
             `Share came back infected` = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * sum(back_inf) / pmax(sum(sent_inf), 1)),
             `Their contagious days at school` = ci(back_contag)),
         by = .(School = school, Strategy = strategy)]
fwrite(r2, file.path(RESULTS_DIR, sprintf("09_R2_per_outbreak_n%d_seed%d.csv", N_RUNS, SEED_BEHAV)))
knitr::kable(r2, align = "llrrrrr",
             caption = "Per outbreak, mean (95% CI) over independent runs. 'Came back still infected' = returned to school latent or contagious at the end of their first stay at home while infected.")
```

**How to read it.** Shorter quarantines send home about the same number of
infected students, but more of them come back still infected and spend
their contagious days at school. These extra contagious days at school are what
make outbreaks larger.

## C4. Students who come back from quarantine still infected

```{r c4, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
c4 <- CD[, { m <- mean(back_inf); h <- 1.96 * sd(back_inf) / sqrt(.N)
             .(mean = m, lo = m - h, hi = m + h) }, by = .(school, strategy)]
p <- ggplot(c4, aes(strategy, mean, fill = strategy)) + geom_col(width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.2) +
  geom_text(aes(y = hi, label = sprintf("%.1f", mean)), vjust = -0.5, size = 3.3) +
  facet_wrap(~school, nrow = 1) + scale_fill_manual(values = COLS) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Students back at school still infected\n(per outbreak, mean and 95% CI)",
       title = "Students who come back from quarantine still infected (latent or contagious)") + th +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
save_fig(p, "09_C4_released_infected.png", 10, 4.5)
```

## C5. How much of the contagious period quarantine covers

```{r c5, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
STAY_LEV <- c("Never home", "1 day", sprintf("2-%d days", MIN_HOME - 1), sprintf("%d-20 days", MIN_HOME), "21+ days")
c5 <- ST[!is.na(contagious) & contagious > 0][, stay_grp := factor(fcase(
  stay == 0, STAY_LEV[1], stay == 1, STAY_LEV[2], stay < MIN_HOME, STAY_LEV[3],
  stay <= 20, STAY_LEV[4], default = STAY_LEV[5]), STAY_LEV)]
c5 <- c5[, .(share = sum(contag_home) / sum(contagious), n = .N), by = .(school, stay_grp)]
p <- ggplot(c5, aes(stay_grp, share)) + geom_col(fill = "#3A7DBA", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%\nn=%d", 100 * share, n)), vjust = -0.2, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~school, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1.2), breaks = seq(0, 1, .25)) +
  labs(x = "Longest stay at home while infected", y = "Share of contagious days spent at home",
       title = "How much of a student's contagious period quarantine covers",
       subtitle = "All strategies pooled; n = infected students") + th +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
save_fig(p, "09_C5_coverage_by_stay.png", 10, 4.5)
```
